P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Yes, but under exchange control. The Office des Changes' General Instruction on Exchange Operations (IGOC 2026) defines a services export as a paid service rendered in Morocco or abroad by a resident to a non-resident. Service exporters must repatriate the FULL proceeds within 90 days of performing the service. The repatriated FX must be sold (converted to dirhams), except for the share that may be placed in an FX or convertible-dirham account (up to 70%, see P2). The Office des Changes has publicly said this 90-day rule applies to online services by resident individuals. It has sanctioned non-repatriation and unauthorised holdings abroad, including balances on PayPal/Payoneer-type platforms.

sources.title: Instruction Générale des Opérations de Change 2026 — 4. Exportation de services
sources.quote: Les exportations de services désignent, au sens de la présente Instruction, les prestations rendues au Maroc ou à l’étranger par un résident en faveur d’un non-résident et donnant lieu à une rémunération.

sources.title: IGOC 2026 — 4.3 Rapatriement du produit des exportations de services
sources.quote: Les exportateurs de services sont tenus de procéder au rapatriement du montant intégral des recettes de leurs exportations conformément aux dispositions de l’article 11 de la présente Instruction et ce, dans un délai de quatre-vingt-dix (90) jours à compter de la date de la réalisation des prestations de services. Les montants rapatriés doivent être cédés, dans les conditions prévues par l’article 22 de la présente Instruction.

P1_fx_receipts.notes: Secondary sites disagreed on the services deadline (90 vs 150 days). The 150 days in IGOC 2026 is for GOODS, counted from the customs declaration; services = 90 days from performance. The Infomédiaire item is a 2022 MAP interview with the Office des Changes Director General; the rule is unchanged in IGOC 2026.

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes, with a cap. IGOC 2026 lets banks open FX or convertible-dirham accounts for Moroccan resident individuals NOT on the commercial register who have foreign-source income. They may credit up to 70% of repatriated foreign-source income, and the remainder must be sold on the FX market. Service exporters on the commercial register have their own exporter FX accounts, also capped at 70% of repatriated proceeds.

P4_paypal.question: Can residents receive money via PayPal?
P4_paypal.answer: Yes, with a local repatriation clause. PayPal's Moroccan user agreement has a Morocco section: once withdrawal to a Moroccan bank account with PayPal's bank partner is enabled, users must comply with Moroccan law. Amounts received from PayPal users must be withdrawn to a Moroccan bank account within 30 days, and the partner bank charges a fee per withdrawal. Since September 2025, PayPal balances can be withdrawn in dirhams through the Cash Plus mobile app (Cash Plus is a payment institution licensed by Bank Al-Maghrib). PayPal's Payouts table lists Morocco as 'Send, receive, and withdraw' (automated collector).

This means notably that if you receive amounts into the balance of your PayPal account from a PayPal user, you must withdraw the amounts in the balance of your PayPal account to your Moroccan bank account* within 30 Days of receipt of funds.

P5_payoneer_wise.question: Payoneer / Wise availability for residents
P5_payoneer_wise.answer: Payoneer: widely used by Moroccan freelancers (receiving accounts in USD/EUR, marketplace integration). A Casablanca chartered-accountant firm stresses it is a collection tool, not an exchange-control exemption: funds must be repatriated to a Moroccan bank account in the professional's name, with records kept. Wise: Morocco is NOT on Wise's list of countries whose residents can hold money, so residents get no Wise balance or account details. One blog's claim that Moroccans can use Wise Business conflicts with Wise's own list and is not relied on. Sending money TO Morocco via Wise is a separate service.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: Simplest form: the auto-entrepreneur status (Law 114-13). Register on the national AE register (rn.ae.gov.ma) and validate at any Barid Al-Maghrib (Poste Maroc) branch with the national ID card (CIN), a photo and proof of address. This gives an RNAE number, ICE and tax ID. Ceilings: MAD 200,000/yr turnover for services and MAD 500,000 for commercial, industrial or craft activities. Exporting services to foreign clients is allowed. Alternatives are a sole proprietorship taxed under IR, or an SARL AU (single-member LLC). Exchange control allows non-RC-registered resident individuals with foreign income to hold FX accounts (P2), so commercial-register registration is not a precondition for receiving foreign income.

L2_tax_id.question: Tax ID: who needs one, how to get it?
L2_tax_id.answer: Anyone carrying on a gainful activity needs a tax identifier (identifiant fiscal, IF) from the DGI. Businesses, including auto-entrepreneurs and self-employed individuals, also get the 15-digit ICE (Identifiant Commun de l'Entreprise), mandatory since 1 July 2016. For auto-entrepreneurs, the ICE and IF are issued automatically with RNAE registration at Barid Al-Maghrib.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Tax residents (permanent home, centre of economic interests, or more than 183 days in any 365-day period) pay income tax (IR) on WORLDWIDE income. The scale since 1 Jan 2025 is: 0% up to MAD 40,000, then 10%, 20%, 30% and 34%, and 37% above MAD 180,000. Auto-entrepreneurs instead pay a final 1% of collected turnover on services (0.5% commercial). Since 1 Jan 2023, an AE's annual services turnover above MAD 80,000 from the SAME client is taxed at a final 30%, withheld by the client.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: The standard VAT rate is 20% (10% reduced). Exported services are exempt WITH the right to deduct input VAT (CGI art. 92-I-1°): no VAT is charged to the foreign client, and input VAT can be deducted or refunded. This requires the service to be used abroad and an invoice in the foreign client's name. Auto-entrepreneurs do not charge VAT. Individual service providers with annual turnover up to MAD 500,000 are exempt without deduction under CGI art. 91-II-3° (single-source, see notes).

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: Law 09-08 (18 Feb 2009) applies to all processing whose controller or means are in Morocco; no replacement law had been adopted by Oct 2026. Every website operator that collects personal data must NOTIFY the CNDP before processing. A prior declaration is the default. Prior AUTHORISATION is needed if national ID (CNI) numbers or sensitive data are processed. Hosting or storing data on servers abroad requires a separate transfer request, filed together with the basic declaration. Users must be informed at collection (controller identity, purposes, recipients, access/rectification rights).

L7_incentives.question: Legal incentives / tax holidays / special zones relevant to small digital businesses
L7_incentives.answer: (1) Auto-entrepreneur regime: final 1% tax on collected service turnover (0.5% commercial), no VAT, simplified records. Watch the MAD 80,000 same-client cap (L3). (2) Exchange-control facilities: individuals keep up to 70% of repatriated foreign income in an FX or convertible-dirham account (P2). The individual 'e-commerce allowance' for paying foreign online services was raised to MAD 20,000/yr in IGOC 2026. (3) Start-ups labelled by the Digital Development Agency (ADD) can invest abroad up to MAD 10m/yr and buy services online via international cards under IGOC 2026. (4) Exported services are VAT-exempt with input-VAT refund rights (L4).

D1_id_document.question: Identity documents residents use for KYC (gateways, banks, platforms)
D1_id_document.answer: The Carte Nationale d'Identité Électronique (CNIE, Law 04-20; new generation issued by the DGSN since 2020) is the standard ID. It is valid for 10 years for over-12s, carries a PIN and supports NFC verification for digital services. Banks register FX allowances on the basis of the CNI. Auto-entrepreneur registration requires a copy of the CIN (both sides). CMI requires the signatory's ID.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Physical or digital goods on Etsy (Etsy seller payments are available here). (5) Client payments by PayPal (on PayPal's Payouts list as 'Send, receive, and withdraw'). (6) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
